subject: en
source: English National Curriculum — English programmes of study: key stage 2 (Year 6), writing composition and English Appendix 2 (vocabulary, grammar and punctuation), DfE 2013

weeks.topic: Narrative: show, not tell, in character description
objectives: Reveal character through actions, speech and thoughts
Avoid simply naming emotions
Choose precise verbs and adverbs

weeks.topic: Subject, object and the active voice
objectives: Identify the subject and object of a sentence
Write sentences in the active voice
Explain who is doing the action
Use the passive voice to affect the presentation of information
Transform active sentences into passive ones
Use the passive in formal and scientific writing
Create a fantasy world with its own rules
Plan a quest with rising action and resolution
Develop a hero and a villain

weeks.topic: Colons, semi-colons and dashes between clauses
objectives: Use semi-colons, colons or dashes to mark the boundary between independent clauses
Explain the difference between each mark
Use them for effect in writing
Use the layout and conventions of a formal letter
Write politely and persuasively in formal register
Organise points into clear paragraphs

weeks.topic: Formal and informal language; the subjunctive
objectives: Recognise vocabulary and structures for formal speech and writing
Use the subjunctive form (e.g. If I were...)
Switch between formal and informal registers
Present both sides of an issue fairly
Support points with evidence
Reach a reasoned conclusion
Link ideas across paragraphs with repetition of a word or phrase
Use adverbials such as on the other hand, in contrast and as a consequence
Use ellipsis to avoid repetition
Identify the features of a ballad
Use a regular rhyme scheme and refrain
Write and perform a ballad

weeks.topic: Journalism: editorials, bias and fact versus opinion
objectives: Distinguish between fact and opinion in news writing
Identify bias in reporting
Write an editorial expressing a view

weeks.topic: Colons and semi-colons in lists; bullet points
objectives: Use a colon to introduce a list
Use semi-colons within lists
Punctuate bullet points consistently

weeks.topic: Writing in the style of an author
objectives: Analyse the style of a chosen author (e.g. Michael Morpurgo)
Imitate sentence structures and vocabulary
Write a new chapter in that style
Use hyphens to avoid ambiguity (e.g. man-eating shark)
Use ellipsis for suspense or omission
Edit writing for precision

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: voice, register and punctuation
objectives: Revisit active and passive voice
Consolidate formal register and the subjunctive
Practise colons, semi-colons and dashes
Compare biography and autobiography
Write an autobiographical extract with reflection
Use a mix of tenses for past and present

weeks.topic: Synonyms, antonyms and shades of meaning
objectives: Explore how words are related as synonyms and antonyms
Choose words to convey precise meaning and tone
Use a thesaurus critically
Explain a scientific process in sequence
Use technical vocabulary and the passive voice
Include diagrams with labels
Tell the same event from two characters' perspectives
Use first and third person narration
Show how viewpoint changes the reader's sympathy
Use headings, sub-headings, columns, bullets and tables to structure text
Choose layout for the reader's needs
Design an information page

weeks.topic: Persuasive campaign on a global issue
objectives: Research a global issue such as plastic pollution
Write a campaign speech or letter
Use statistics and rhetorical devices

weeks.topic: Shakespeare retold: narrative from a scene
objectives: Explore a Shakespeare play in a child-friendly version (e.g. Macbeth)
Retell a key scene as a narrative
Use dialogue inspired by the play
Identify extended metaphors in poems
Sustain one metaphor through a poem
Evaluate how poets create meaning
Write a formal non-chronological report
Use impersonal constructions and the passive
Include a glossary of technical terms
Use dialogue to advance the action
Integrate speech with description of action
Punctuate complex speech accurately

weeks.topic: Descriptive writing: atmosphere and pathetic fallacy
objectives: Create atmosphere using weather and setting
Use pathetic fallacy to reflect mood
Vary sentence length for effect

weeks.topic: Mock assessment: grammar, punctuation, spelling and writing
objectives: Complete a GPS test under timed conditions
Write an independent piece
Identify targets for revision

weeks.topic: GPS revision: word classes and sentence types
objectives: Revisit word classes, clauses and phrases
Practise statement, question, command and exclamation
Use correct terminology in test answers
Revisit all KS2 punctuation marks
Practise apostrophes, commas and inverted commas
Explain punctuation choices
Plan and write a narrative independently
Show a range of Year 6 features
Edit and improve without adult support
Choose a non-fiction form for a purpose and audience
Write independently with appropriate register
Evaluate and improve the piece
Explore how films tell stories with shots and scenes
Write a short screenplay
Create a storyboard to match
Write a memoir about memorable experiences
Use reflective language and detail
Read aloud a leavers' speech
Choose poems around a theme
Write an introduction to the anthology
Perform poems with expression
Write a point supported by evidence and explanation
Use quotations accurately
Analyse the effect of language

weeks.topic: End-of-year assessment: Year 6 writing and grammar
objectives: Write an independent piece showing Year 6 features
Complete a final grammar and punctuation check
Reflect on progress

weeks.topic: Year 6 review and transition to secondary
objectives: Reflect on progress in English
Set targets for Year 7
Celebrate published writing
